summary: The new lead-in chamfer is on the correct face. I sliced the built bracket: the window is 42.28 x 21.79 mm at the back face (y = 0), narrows at 45 degrees to the nominal 41.3 x 20.6 mm by y = 0.5, and stays nominal through to the front face. The back face is both the entry face for the top-first servo and the face that sits on the bed (print_rot [90,0,0] puts the 7198 mm^2 back face on the bed), so the chamfer guides the case in and absorbs elephant's foot where it occurs. The rebuild is clean: no interference, all 12 M3 fasteners aligned, the +/-90 deg sweep is clear, and arm_torque, both FEA cases and rig_mass pass. The renders show nothing wrong. Four of the five earlier findings are resolved; what remains is minor (engine access checks still missing, and the chamfer thins the pilot-hole wall at the bed face).

findings.issue: Still open from the last review (engine half): nothing in the engine checks assembly access. I re-probed the current assembly. A straight 3 mm hex key on the two cable-end tab screw axes (x = +24.75, z = 78 and 88) still overlaps the servo's cable boss by 3.1 mm^3 each; the far-end screws are clear. DESIGN.md step 3 now says to use a ball-end driver there, so this project is covered. But kerf check would not catch the same problem, or a bottom-first servo that cannot pass its window, on the next project. The pilot-material, top_through and part-notes tests from the earlier finding are now in tests/test_iface.py (resolved).
findings.fix: Finish the open PLAN item 'Assembly-access checks': (a) sweep a hex-key cylinder along each male fastener axis from the head side and report screws that need a ball-end driver; (b) sweep parts that declare an `insert:` path into their seat and report collisions. Test both: this rig's cable-end screws must be flagged as ball-end, and a bottom-first MG996R through a tight window must fail.

findings.issue: New: the lead-in chamfer thins the wall between the window and the tab pilot holes at the back face. The pilot holes are 2.60 mm at x = +/-24.75, so their inner edges are at |x| = 23.45. Deeper than 0.5 mm the window edge is at 20.65 and leaves a 2.8 mm wall; at the back face the chamfer moves the window edge to 21.1, leaving 2.35 mm. That is just under the 2.4 mm boss-wall guideline (ENGINEERING section 5), over only the first ~0.5 mm (2-3 layers) of the bed face, which is exactly where the thread-forming screw starts and pushes plastic outward. The risk is low: the tab clamps that zone, and the 7.2 mm of thread behind it is unchanged. But the engine applied the chamfer without checking the wall it leaves.
findings.fix: In iface.servo_mount, limit lead_in to keep at least 2.4 mm between the chamfered window edge and the female hole edges (here at most 0.45 mm per side on the ends), or leave the chamfer off the two short ends next to the tab holes and keep it on the long sides. Add a test that checks the remaining wall.

findings.issue: Still open, carried over: the catalog still marks the tab-hole pattern (49.5 x 10 mm, 4.2 mm holes) and the cable-boss geometry UNVERIFIED for this servo. The ball-end driver note and the boss clearance depend on them. DESIGN.md's caliper note now covers both the tab holes and the boss (the documentation half of the earlier finding is resolved).
findings.fix: When a real MG996R is in hand, measure the tab-hole pattern and the boss, record them in catalog/hardware.json with the measurement as the source, and rebuild.
